text: TFTips - Privacy Policy 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Privacy Policy Introduction This website respects the privacy of our users and is committed to protecting personal information. This privacy policy explains what information we collect and how we use it. Information We Collect We may collect the following information: Anonymized usage statistics for access analysis (Google Analytics) Interaction recordings on some pages (Microsoft Clarity); text and input are masked Cookie information for site functionality improvement Local storage information for saving user preferences How We Use Information The collected information is used for the following purposes: Improving site content and functionality Access analysis and statistics Saving and restoring user preferences Third-Party Services We use the following third-party services: Google Analytics - Access analysis (anonymized data only) Google AdSense - Ad delivery (hidden for Patreon supporters) YouTube - Video embedding (YouTube's privacy policy applies) Patreon - Supporter authentication (Patreon's privacy policy applies) Third-Party Data Sharing We do not sell, rent, or provide user personal information to third parties except as required by law. However, when using the third-party services mentioned above, data is processed according to each service's terms of use. About Cookies We use cookies to improve user experience. Cookies are small text files stored in your browser. You can refuse cookies through your browser settings, but this may limit some site functionality. Types of cookies we use: Essential Cookies: Required for basic site functionality (authentication, language settings, etc.) Analytics Cookies: To understand site usage (Google Analytics) Session Recording Cookies: To record interactions on some pages for usability improvements (Microsoft Clarity) Functional Cookies: To save user preferences (theme, display settings, etc.) You can manage cookie acceptance through your browser settings. About User Authentication We provide login functionality using Patreon authentication. This feature is used to provide benefits such as ad-free browsing to those who support our site on Patreon. During login, we receive public information provided by Patreon (username, email address, etc.). We do not store passwords on our site. Patreon Integration Details Information obtained during Patreon login: User ID, username, email address, profile picture Pledge status (whether currently supporting) Patreon Privacy Policy: https://www.patreon.com/policy/privacy Security We manage collected information appropriately and take reasonable security measures to prevent unauthorized access, loss, damage, alteration, or leakage. Specific security measures: SSL/TLS encryption for secure communications Regular software updates and security patches Restricted and monitored administrator access External Links This site may contain links to external sites. Please check the privacy policy of each linked site. Log Files We follow a standard procedure of using log files. These files log visitors when they visit websites. The information collected by log files includes internet protocol (IP) addresses, browser type, Internet Service Provider (ISP), date and time stamp, referring/exit pages, and possibly the number of clicks. These are not linked to any information that is personally identifiable. The purpose of the information is for analyzing trends, administering the site, tracking users' movement on the website, and gathering demographic information. Data Protection Rights You are entitled to the following rights: The right to access - You have the right to request copies of your personal data. The right to rectification - You have the right to request that we correct any information you believe is inaccurate. The right to erasure - You have the right to request that we erase your personal data, under certain conditions. The right to restrict processing - You have the right to request that we restrict the processing of your personal data, under certain conditions. The right to data portability - You have the right to request that we transfer the data to another organization. If you make a request, we have one month to respond to you. Compliance with Japanese Privacy Law This site complies with the Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI) of Japan and handles personal information appropriately. The acquisition, use, provision, and management of personal information are conducted in accordance with applicable laws. Data Retention Period We retain collected personal information for the following periods: Access analytics data: 26 months (Google Analytics default setting) Interaction recordings: 30 days (Microsoft Clarity default setting) Account information: 2 years from last login After the retention period expires, data will be promptly deleted or anonymized. Use by Minors This site is intended for users aged 13 and above. Users under 13 should not provide personal information without parental consent. If we become aware that we have collected personal information from a user under 13, we will promptly delete it. Changes to Privacy Policy We may change this privacy policy as needed. Any changes will be notified on this page. Contact Us If you have any questions about our privacy policy, please contact us at @tft_ips . title: TFTips - SET18 "Enchanted Wilds" Overview 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - SET18 "Enchanted Wilds" Overview 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays SET18 "Enchanted Wilds" Overview The latest set, set in an enchanted forest Contents About Enchanted Wilds Schedule New Mechanic: Wisps Migration to the Unreal Engine Changes from SET17 Official Video About Enchanted Wilds Schedule New Mechanic: Wisps Migration to the Unreal Engine Changes from SET17 Official Video * Based on the PBE build. Numbers and behavior can still change before the live release. About Enchanted Wilds SET18 "Enchanted Wilds" is a new set themed around magical forests and fairy tales. Themed around a mystical forest and the spirits that dwell within it The new Wisps mechanic adds fresh choices to the shop TFT moves to the Unreal Engine for the first time in its history Schedule PBE start July 28 To stabilize the new engine, the PBE runs for four weeks instead of the usual two. Live release August 26 Launches with patch 18.1. SET17 is extended until this date. New Mechanic: Wisps The centerpiece of SET18 is the new Wisps mechanic — an evolution of the Charms from SET12. Appears in the rightmost shop slot every other round You can buy up to one per round; a single-use effect that temporarily boosts combat, economy, items, and more They grow stronger and more expensive as the game goes on; from Stage 5, combat-focused Wisps alternate in 177 Wisps span categories like Champion, Combat, Shop, and Gold/XP The Blossom trait empowers your Wisps: (5) makes one appear every round, (7) refunds 5 gold per purchase, and (9) lets you buy two per round See the full list with appearance stages * Effects and prices come from the PBE build and may be tuned before the live release. Migration to the Unreal Engine SET18 is the first set where TFT moves to the Unreal Engine. It replaces the Hextech engine used since 2019 and brings a few changes to how you play. The initial download is significantly larger (later patches return to normal sizes) Preferred settings and favorited cosmetics are reset during the engine migration The minimap is removed (a reworked Pings feature is planned for the future) Higher system requirements — 2GB+ RAM on iOS, 2–3GB+ on Android, and Windows 10 (19041+) with DirectX 11 on PC On PC you keep launching TFT from the League of Legends client until the dedicated client arrives on October 9 (the game itself moves to Unreal at the live release) On mobile the TFT app is replaced with the Unreal version automatically, so there is no separate client to wait for Your Riot account, RP, and TFT-specific currencies carry over unchanged. Changes from SET17 SET17's "Realm of the Gods" mechanic ends. God alignments and Boons were a SET17-only system. Augment rotations and other system changes are due from Riot separately before the live release Official Video TFT Dev Drop: Enchanted Wilds Riot's official set reveal video, showcasing new champions, traits, Wisps, and more. title: TFTips - Augments - Game Specs & Rules 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Augments - Game Specs & Rules 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Augments Augment Ranks Augments come in three ranks: Silver , Gold , and Prismatic . All players select one augment of the same rank in the same round (usually 2-1, 3-2, 4-2). Three augments are offered, and each can be rerolled (swapped for another of the same rank). Augment Tree Augment tier (Silver, Gold, Prismatic) appearance rates follow fixed patterns determined per game. By knowing your first augment tier (at 2-1), you can partially predict future augment tiers. Using the tree below, if your first augment is Prismatic , the second augment (3-2) will be Silver 50%, Gold 30%, Prismatic 20%. Silver Gold Prismatic 26 36 50 5 50 5 61 71 11 30 5 4 100 1 65 28 90 16 10 2 48 65 20 35 11 24 35 5 59 9 6 1 9 51 80 4 20 1 30 67 2 33 1 20 50 1 50 1 (Values are in % ) Augment Selection Mechanism Each augment has specific rounds where it can or cannot appear. (e.g., In SET14, Crest augments only appear at 2-1) At rounds 3-2 and 4-2, your board state from the previous round is referenced and influences the augment choices offered to you. The exact factors considered are not officially stated, but at least active traits are relevant. Any augment that appeared in your choices during the game will not appear again in later selections, even if you did not pick it. title: TFTips - Battle - Game Specs & Rules 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Battle - Game Specs & Rules 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Battle Damage Types and Formulas How Damage Is Calculated Physical and magic damage taken is the base damage multiplied by the following factors. Base damage × Crit Damage × Damage Amp × Resistance × Damage Reduction Crit Damage only applies when the hit crits. Every factor is a multiplier, so the order does not matter. Damage Amp only applies to units' basic attacks and abilities. Damage from items, traits, augments, and wisps is not amplified. Damage Types Type Reduced by Physical damage Armor and Damage Reduction Magic damage Magic Resist and Damage Reduction True damage Not reduced by Armor, Magic Resist, or Damage Reduction However, if the target takes more than 1× damage (for example from Vulnerable), true damage is increased by the same multiplier. Reduction from Armor and Magic Resist Physical damage taken = 100 Armor + 100 × Original Physical damage Magic damage taken = 100 Magic Resist + 100 × Original Magic damage At 100 Armor or Magic Resist, damage taken is halved. At 200, it drops to one third. Damage Reduction Damage left after Armor or Magic Resist is reduced further by Damage Reduction . Final damage taken = Damage after resistances × 100 − Damage Reduction 100 Multiple Damage Reduction sources do not add up. The portions of damage that get through are multiplied. Example: two 50% sources let 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25 of the damage through, which is 75% Damage Reduction in total. When the target is Vulnerable (a debuff that increases damage taken), Vulnerable is added after all Damage Reduction is applied. Example: with 20% Damage Reduction and 10% Vulnerable, damage taken is 0.8 + 0.1 = 0.9×, not 0.8 × 1.1 = 0.88×. Worked example Physical damage of 100 against a unit with Armor 50 and Damage Reduction 20%: Reduced by 50 Armor: 100 × 100 ÷ (50 + 100) ≈ 66.7 Reduced by 20% Damage Reduction: 66.7 × 0.8 ≈ 53.3 The target takes about 53.3, roughly half of the base damage. Shields and Health A target with 200 health and a 30 shield takes 100 damage after reductions: Damage 100 Health left 130 Health -70 Shield -30 Shields take damage first, and the rest reduces health. With multiple shields, the one with the least time left is used first. Other Rules Omnivamp heals only from damage that reduced the target's health. Damage absorbed by shields does not count. Only basic attacks can be dodged. Damage from abilities, items, and traits cannot be dodged. Units on the team that won the fight stop at 1 health and do not die, even if damage such as Burn continues after the fight is decided. Debuffs Main debuffs that items and abilities put on enemies. Crowd Control Debuffs that temporarily stop basic attacks, abilities, or movement. They stop working 8 seconds into overtime. Name Effect Stun Stops basic attacks, abilities, and movement. Mana does not increase while stunned. Knockup Launches the target into the air. It cannot act for the duration. Slow Reduce Attack Speed Disarmed Cannot attack Other Debuffs Name Effect Value from items Sunder Reduce Armor 30% Shred Reduce Magic Resist 30% Wound Reduces healing received 33% Burn Deals a percent of the target’s max Health as true damage every second 1% Mana Reave Increase the Mana cost of the next Ability cast - Vulnerable Increases damage taken - Only listed when every item applies the same value. Abilities and traits may apply different values. Effects that lower Armor or Magic Resist by a flat amount are calculated separately from Sunder and Shred. If both apply, both take effect. When the same debuff from the table above is applied more than once, only the one with the highest value takes effect. If the values are equal, the one with more time left takes effect, so reapplying works like extending the duration. Basic Attack Targeting How Targets Are Picked The target is basically the closest enemy. It is picked at the start of combat and re-picked after every hex moved until it is in range. A new target is also picked when the target dies, leaves range, or becomes untargetable. Closeness is compared by the hexes walked to reach an attack position, then hex distance, then the straight-line distance between centers (actual distance). If all are tied, the enemy with higher targeting priority is chosen. Tank units have high targeting priority and Assassin units low. Units that become untargetable by enemies are also dropped from the candidates. Examples: When a Tank stands next to the closest enemy After an enemy is picked, enemies on hexes next to it are compared again. This re-check looks at targeting priority before actual distance, so the target can switch to a slightly farther Tank. Tank A Self Range 4 example. Both can be hit without moving, and both are 4 hexes away. The first comparison picks A, which is closer in actual distance: A is 3.46 hexes away, Tank is 3.61. Tank is next to A, so it enters the re-check and wins on targeting priority. Placing a Tank next to an ally the enemy would target, at the same hex distance from that enemy, tends to draw long-range attacks onto the Tank. The target stays until it leaves range While the current target is in range, the unit keeps it. Range has a small margin, so the unit keeps attacking even if the target steps slightly out of range. Whether an attack reaches depends only on the distance between the two units' centers. A unit's visual size does not change range, whether it is attacking or being attacked. How the target is picked in detail In the first comparison, candidates are compared in this order, and the first difference decides. Fewer hexes to move to an attack position Closer in hexes Closer in actual distance Higher targeting priority In front of the unit Same as the previous target Three ways to measure closeness Movement steps, hex distance, and actual distance can differ for the same two units. 4 4 A 3 4 4 4 2 Ally Ally Ally 3 4 1 Self 1 2 3 4 Movement steps: 4 How many hexes the unit walks before it can attack. Hexes with other units are blocked, so detours count. A 2 2 1 1 Self Hex distance: 3 How many hexes apart, ignoring units. Movement is compared first, so enemy B is chosen. Overtime 30 seconds into combat, overtime starts (up to 15 seconds). During overtime, every unit's movement speed increases by 700 (normally 500). Roles indicate a champion's basic combat style and are an important factor when building team compositions. title: TFTips - Stats - Game Specs & Rules 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Stats - Game Specs & Rules 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Stats Stats Overview Champions have various stats that determine their combat performance. Items, traits, and augments can enhance these stats. Stat Name Base Value Description Health Unit-specific Health. The unit is defeated when this reaches 0. Max Mana Unit-specific Mana required to cast the ability. Starting Mana Unit-specific Mana at the start of combat. Mana Regen 0 Mana passively regenerated over time. Base AD Unit-specific Damage dealt by basic attacks. Attack Damage 0% Increases base attack damage and some ability damage. Ability Power 0% Affects ability damage and effects. Attack Speed Unit-specific Number of basic attacks per second. Capped at 5.0 by default. Range Unit-specific Number of hexes basic attacks can reach. Armor Unit-specific Reduces physical damage taken. Magic Resist Unit-specific Reduces magic damage taken. Damage Reduction 0% Reduces all damage taken. Crit Chance 25% Chance for basic attacks to critically strike. Crit Damage 140% Total damage dealt on critical strike. Omnivamp 0% Recovers a percentage of damage dealt as health. Damage Amp 0% Increases all damage dealt. Star Level Collect 3 of the same 1-star champion to level up to 2-star, and collect 3 of the same 2-star champion to reach 3-star. When star level increases by 1, Base AD becomes 1.5x, Health becomes 1.8x (with exceptions), and skill effects increase. Separately, high-cost units at 3-star or above gain flat Health : +1000 at cost 4 / +5000 at cost 5. Cost 1 units can always be sold for the same gold they cost to purchase regardless of star level, but Cost 2+ units at 2-star or 3-star receive 1 less gold when sold. Mana Mana is a resource required to cast abilities. Units start combat with a set amount of starting mana and automatically cast their ability upon reaching max mana. Mana-Related Stats Max Mana The mana threshold needed to cast an ability. Varies by champion. Starting Mana Mana held at the start of combat. Can be increased by items and augments. Mana Regen Mana passively regenerated over time. Mana Gain Mechanics Roles , units gain mana from basic attacks. Items and augments can also provide additional mana. Only Tank units gain mana from taking damage. Each hit grants 1% of the damage before mitigation (up to 50) plus 3% of the damage after mitigation (up to 50). Damage absorbed by a Shield still counts. Some champions (Specialists) do not use mana and have their own unique resource system. Mana Lock Most units are in a "mana lock" state while casting their ability and cannot gain mana. The lock ends when the ability finishes. Mana gained beyond the maximum on the attack that fills the bar is not lost; it is returned when the mana lock ends. Stun stops new attacks and abilities, but does not interrupt an ability that has already started. Critical Strike Critical strikes occur with a set probability on basic attacks, amplifying damage. With the right items and augments, you can achieve high burst damage. Critical Strike Stats Crit Rate Chance for basic attacks to critically strike. Base value is 25%. Crit Damage Damage multiplier on critical strike. Base value is 140% (1.4x). Base Mechanics Stat Base Value Description Crit Rate 25% Same starting value for all champions Crit Damage 140% 1.4x normal damage Applies to Basic attacks Only basic attacks by default Crit Chance Over 100% Behavior Crit Chance exceeds 100%, the excess is converted to Crit Damage at a 50% rate. Bonus Crit Damage = ( Crit Chance - 100%) × 0.5 Example: Crit Chance at 110% Excess 10% x 0.5 = 5% added to Crit Damage overflowCalcAfter Final Crit Damage : 140% + 5% = 145% Ability Critical Strikes Normally, critical strikes only apply to basic attacks, but certain items, augments and traits can enable ability critical strikes. Damage That Cannot Crit Some damage, such as from the items below or burn, can never critically strike. title: TFTips - Wisps - Game Specs & Rules 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Wisps - Game Specs & Rules 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Wisps When Wisps Appear During the planning phase of a PvP round, a wisp appears every second shop you roll. The shop at the start of the round counts as a roll. 1st 2nd 3rd 4th Wisps do not appear during the planning phase of PvE rounds. The wisp takes the rightmost shop slot. When you buy a wisp, its slot is refilled with a champion rolled at your level at that moment. Level up first, and the slot is rolled at the new level. Only one wisp is in the shop at a time. You can buy one per round; after buying, no more appear that round. While Blossom is active, wisps appear more often and you can buy more per round. When the planning phase ends, unbought wisps disappear and are replaced by champions, even if the shop is locked. The shop count since the last wisp does not reset between rounds. If you rerolled once after a wisp appeared last round, the first shop of the next round is your 2nd, so a wisp appears there. How Wisps Are Chosen The wisp is picked at random from those that meet all of the following. It meets its stage window and its own conditions. See the wisp list It is not on cooldown (after appearing in your shop, it cannot appear again until 5 other Wisps have been offered, about 10 shops since a Wisp appears every 2 shops; some Wisps have longer cooldowns). Its price is at most the gold you have now. Beggar's Wisp only appears when no other wisp can be offered (for example, you lack the gold or none meet their conditions). text: TFTips - SET1 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Back to Timeline SET1 The set that started it all. Unit placement, item crafting, and trait synergies — the foundational mechanics every set since has built on — were all established here. It launched using existing League of Legends champions with no set-specific theme. Champions Traits Articles Tier 1 Tier 1 Camille Hextech Blademaster The Hextech Ultimatum Camille singles out and leaps on an enemy, dealing 200/325/450 magic damage and rooting them for 4/5/6 seconds. Allies within range will prioritize attacking Camille's target. Darius Imperial Knight Decimate Darius swings his axe in a circle, dealing 150/200/250 magic damage and healing himself for 100/150/200 health for each enemy hit. Elise Demon Shapeshifter Spider Form Elise transforms into a giant spider and summons 1/2/4 spiderlings to fight alongside her. While in spider form, Elise gains bonus lifesteal. Spiderlings benefit from active Demon trait bonuses. Fiora Noble Blademaster Riposte Fiora enters a defensive stance for 1.5 seconds, becoming immune to damage and enemy spell effects. As she exits this stance, she ripostes, dealing 100/250/400 magic damage to a nearby enemy and stunning them for 1.5 seconds. Garen Noble Knight Judgement Garen spins his sword for 4 seconds, becoming immune to magic damage and dealing magic damage to nearby enemies over the duration. Graves Pirate Gunslinger Buckshot Passive: Graves' basic attacks deal 5% bonus physical damage and hit all enemies in a cone in front of him. Graves applies on-hit effects to all enemies hit. Kassadin Void Sorcerer Nether Blade Passive: Kassadin's basic attacks steal 25/50/75 mana from his target and grant him a damage shield for 4 seconds. Kha'Zix Void Assassin Taste their Fear Kha'Zix slashes the nearest enemy, dealing 150/250/350 magic damage. If the enemy has no adjacent teammates, this damage is increased to 400/600/800. Mordekaiser Phantom Knight Obliterate Mordekaiser slams his mace on the two spaces in front of him, dealing 250/500/750 magic damage to enemies within. Nidalee Wild Shapeshifter Primal Surge Nidalee heals herself and an ally, restoring health over 6 seconds, then transforms into cat form. While in cat form, Nidalee's range is reduced to 1 hex and she gains 20/70/120 Bonus Attack Damage. Tristana Yordle Gunslinger Explosive Charge Tristana places a bomb on her current target which will detonate after she Basic Attacks them 3 times or 4 seconds pass without Tristana attacking them. When the bomb detonates, it deals magic damage to all nearby enemies, plus for each Basic Attack, up to a maximum of . Vayne Noble Ranger Silver Bolts Passive: Whenever Vayne Basic Attacks the same target 3 times, she deals of her target's Maximum Health as true damage. Warwick Wild Brawler Infinite Duress Warwick pounces on the weakest enemy, stunning them for 1.5 seconds and striking them 3 times, dealing magic damage. Each strike triggers on-hit effects and heals Warwick for 100% of the damage dealt. Tier 2 Tier 2 Ahri Wild Sorcerer Orb of Deception Ahri fires an orb in a line, dealing 100/200/300 magic damage to all enemies it passes through. It then returns to her, dealing 100/200/300 true damage to all enemies it passes through. Blitzcrank Robot Brawler Rocket Grab Blitzcrank pulls the furthest enemy to him, dealing 250/550/850 magic damage and stunning them for 2.5 seconds. His next attack after pulling knocks up for 1 second. Allies within range will prioritize attacking Blitzcrank's target. Braum Glacial Guardian Unbreakable Braum puts up his shield for 4 seconds, absorbing and stopping all incoming missiles and reducing his damage taken from that direction by 70/80/90%. Jayce Hextech Shapeshifter Transform Mercury Cannon Jayce knocks a nearby enemy away, dealing 200/350/500 magic damage and stunning them for 2.5/4.25/6 seconds. He then transforms into cannon form and gains max attack speed for his next 3/5/7 Basic Attacks. While in cannon form, Jayce's Attack Range is increased by 3 hexes. Lissandra Glacial Elementalist Frozen Tomb Lissandra encases an enemy in ice, stunning them for 1.5 seconds and dealing 175/325/475 magic damage to all enemies in the surrounding area. If she is below health, Lissandra instead encases herself, becoming untargetable for 2 seconds and dealing 175/325/475 magic damage to all enemies in the surrounding area. Lucian Noble Gunslinger Relentless Pursuit Lucian dashes away from his current target, then Basic Attacks them and fires a second shot which deals magic damage. Lulu Yordle Sorcerer Wild Growth Lulu makes 1/2/3 allies giant, granting them 300/400/500 bonus health and knocking up adjacent enemies near them for 1.25 seconds. Pyke Pirate Assassin Phantom Undertow Pyke leaves an afterimage at his location, then dashes behind the farthest enemy. After 1 second, his afterimage returns to Pyke, dealing 150/200/250 magic damage to all enemies it passes through and stunning them for 1.5/2/2.5 seconds. Rek'Sai Void Brawler Burrow Rek'Sai burrows, becoming untargetable for 1 second and healing for health. She emerges at her target, dealing magic damage and knocking them up for 1.75 seconds. Shen Ninja Blademaster Spirit's Refuge Shen creates a zone around himself for 3/4/5 seconds, granting all nearby allies 100% chance to dodge incoming basic attacks. Twisted Fate Pirate Sorcerer Pick a Card Twisted Fate randomly picks a card, then throws it at his current target, dealing magic damage and creating a special effect based on the color of the card. Blue: Restores 30/50/70 mana to all allies adjacent to Twisted Fate. Red: Deals to all enemies adjacent to the target. Gold: Stuns the target for 2/3/4 seconds. Varus Demon Ranger Piercing Arrow Varus channels for 1.5 seconds, then fires a piercing arrow, dealing 300/550/800 magic damage to all enemies in its path. Zed Ninja Assassin Razor Shuriken Zed throws a shuriken in a line, dealing 200/350/500 magic damage to all enemies in its path. Tier 3 Tier 3 Aatrox Demon Blademaster The Darkin Blade Aatrox cleaves the area in front of him, dealing 300/600/900 magic damage to all enemies within. Ashe Glacial Ranger Enchanted Crystal Arrow Ashe fires an arrow at the farthest enemy. It stops on the first target hit, dealing 200/400/600 magic damage and stunning them for 1/1.5/2 seconds per Hex traveled. Evelynn Demon Assassin Last Caress Evelynn deals 200/300/400 magic damage to up to 3 nearby enemies, then teleports away. This damage is increased to against targets below health. Gangplank Pirate Gunslinger Blademaster Powder Kegs Passive: Gangplank periodically places barrels near enemies. Active: Gangplank shoots his barrels, causing them all to explode, dealing 150/250/350 magic damage to nearby enemies and applying on-hit effects. Katarina Imperial Assassin Death Lotus Katarina channels for 2.5 seconds, throwing knives at 4/6/8 nearby enemies, dealing magic damage over the duration and reducing healing by 80% to her targets for 3 seconds. Kennen Ninja Yordle Elementalist Slicing Maelstrom Kennen summons a storm around himself for 3 seconds, calling down lightning bolts on all enemies in the area every 0.5 second and dealing 225/450/675 magic damage over the duration. Each enemy struck by 3 lightning bolts is stunned for 1.5 seconds. Morgana Demon Sorcerer Soul Shackles Morgana fires chains to all nearby enemies, dealing 175/300/425 magic damage. After 3 seconds, all chained enemies still within range of Morgana are stunned for 2/4/6 seconds and take 175/300/425 magic damage again. Poppy Yordle Knight Keeper's Verdict Poppy creates a shockwave in a straight line that can hit up to 1/2/3 enemies, dealing magic damage, knocking up and stunning them for 2/3/4 seconds. title: TFTips - Don't buy XP in 1-cost reroll comps until you hit your 3* units 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Don't buy XP in 1-cost reroll comps until you hit your 3* units 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Don't buy XP in 1-cost reroll comps until you hit your 3* units Intermediate Leveling What In 1-cost reroll comps, do not buy XP until your key units hit 3*. Why Lower player levels offer the highest shop odds for low-cost units. Leveling up too early dilutes your shop pool and lowers those odds, making it much harder to find enough copies to hit your 3* upgrades. How Prioritize building up to 50 gold first, then slow roll above 50 gold to maintain maximum interest. As soon as you hit your 3* units, start spending your gold to buy XP and push levels. title: TFTips - Level to 6 on 3-2 and stabilize your board in 2-cost reroll comps 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Level to 6 on 3-2 and stabilize your board in 2-cost reroll comps 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Level to 6 on 3-2 and stabilize your board in 2-cost reroll comps Intermediate 2-Cost Reroll Leveling What In 2-cost reroll comps, level up to 6 on 3-2 and roll until your key units (the ones holding items) hit 2*. Why This creates a power spike in Stage 3 to protect your HP. If you've been lose streaking in Stage 2, you want to start winstreaking in Stage 3. 3-2 is a natural leveling point where you waste minimal gold on XP. Since this is also an augment round, you have multiple options available to strengthen your board. title: TFTips - Push level 8 on 4-2 to stabilize your board in 4-cost comps 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Push level 8 on 4-2 to stabilize your board in 4-cost comps 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Push level 8 on 4-2 to stabilize your board in 4-cost comps Intermediate Leveling What In 4-cost comps, level up to 8 on 4-2 and roll until your key (item-holding) units are 2*. Why Hitting a power spike in Stage 4 helps you preserve HP and avoid taking heavy player damage. 4-2 is also a clean XP breakpoint, making it the most gold-efficient timing to level up without wasting gold on awkward XP amounts. Since you also receive an augment on this round, you have plenty of flexible options to strengthen your board. Tips Try to secure at least one econ augment to fund your level 8 push and roll down. title: TFTips - Build a Wound (healing reduction) item 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Build a Wound (healing reduction) item 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Build a Wound (healing reduction) item Intermediate Items What Build one item that applies Wound. You can choose between for tanks and or for carries, so pick whichever fits the components you have. Why Enemy frontline units, especially fighters, often rely on heavy sustain and healing. Without healing reduction, they can easily heal through your damage and become almost impossible to bring down, stalling out the entire fight. Tips The Wound effect does not stack, so if you already have one source on your board, focus on building other items instead. title: TFTips - Avoid contested comps 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Avoid contested comps 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Avoid contested comps Beginner Comp What Play comps that other players aren't playing or are unlikely to play. Why This increases your chances of finding the units you need. All players share one unit pool, and the total number of each unit type in the pool is fixed. When other players hold copies of a unit, it becomes harder for you to find that unit in your shop. Tips Don't avoid contested comps too much. If you're in a better position (more gold, better augments, etc.), go ahead and play it anyway. Depending on the meta, when one comp is too strong, 2-3 players can sometimes play it successfully. The longer your carry survives, the more damage they can deal. text: TFTips - Don't hold more than 3 components 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Don't hold more than 3 components Intermediate Items What Make completed items so you're always holding 3 or fewer components. When you're winstreaking, slam items as much as possible. Why Slamming items converts them into board strength and protects your HP. Even if you have upgraded units, you can still lose to opponents who have more completed items on their board. How Know which items your comp's main carries can use. This gives you options to slam items even when you can't build BIS. text: TFTips - Stack 3 items on one unit 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Stack 3 items on one unit Intermediate Items What Stack 3 items on a single unit instead of spreading them across multiple units. If you have 6 items, giving 3 items to 2 units is much stronger than giving 2 items to 3 units. Why Item effects scale multiplicatively, meaning each additional item becomes more valuable the more you stack them on the same unit. Adding a third item to a unit that already holds two yields the biggest power spike. text: TFTips - Apply Shred and healing reduction to your carry's targets 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Apply Shred and healing reduction to your carry's targets Intermediate Positioning Items What Position units holding Shred/Break items or healing reduction (Wound) items on the same side (left or right) as your main carry. Why Break, Shred, and Wound debuffs only matter once they've dealt damage to enemies. If you place these units far from your main carry, your carry will end up attacking high-armor enemies or enemies that keep healing, making it much harder to secure kills and win fights. title: TFTips - Commit to a Winstreak or Losestreak in the Early Game 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Commit to a Winstreak or Losestreak in the Early Game 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Commit to a Winstreak or Losestreak in the Early Game Beginner Economy Progression What Once you start a winstreak or losestreak in the early game, commit to that momentum instead of alternating between wins and losses. Why Maintaining a streak grants up to +3 bonus gold every round. Alternating between wins and losses resets your streak repeatedly, which leaves you with zero streak bonus and puts your econ far behind the rest of the lobby. How When winstreaking, build a board strong enough to keep winning, even if it means sacrificing an interest breakpoint. When losestreaking, avoid spending gold on your board and bank as much econ as possible. Once you hit a 2-round losestreak, decide whether to commit to the full streak or stabilize your board to preserve HP. Tips Streak gold also applies during PvE rounds like 2-7. text: TFTips - Check your upcoming opponents 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Check your upcoming opponents Intermediate Scouting What Before finalizing your positioning, scout the boards of players you might face next. Why Scouting allows you to adjust your positioning to counter enemy setups and judge whether you need to spend gold to upgrade your board. Tweaking your positioning based on your opponent can swing close fights in your favor and save crucial HP throughout the game. How You can identify potential opponents by the matchmaking icons shown next to their names on the player list on the right side of the screen. Click on a player to scout their board. Tips Matchmaking is not completely random; it follows specific rules, such as preventing you from fighting players you faced recently. You only need to scout the players marked with an icon. title: TFTips - Build a Sunder or Shred item 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Build a Sunder or Shred item 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Build a Sunder or Shred item Intermediate Items What Build one item that applies Sunder if your team's main damage is AD, or Shred if your team deals mostly AP. You can choose between tank options like and or carry options like and depending on your available components. Why These items reduce defenses by a percentage, allowing your team to cut through durable frontline tanks much faster. Without Sunder or Shred, heavily armored or high-MR tanks can easily stall your carries and soak up massive amounts of damage. Tips These effects do not stack, so if you already have a source of Sunder or Shred, look to build other items instead. text: TFTips - Slam all components into completed items on 5-1 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Slam all components into completed items on 5-1 Beginner Items What On 5-1, slam all your components into completed items. After Stage 5, components no longer drop from PvE rounds, making them extremely difficult to obtain. By slamming everything on 5-1, you maximize your board strength when it matters most. title: TFTips - Spend all your gold when low on HP 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Spend all your gold when low on HP 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Spend all your gold when low on HP Beginner Economy What Spend all your gold once your HP drops to around 30. Why Once you are eliminated, any unspent gold is completely wasted and does nothing to improve your placement. In the late game, a single loss can cost you 10 or more HP, meaning 30 HP puts you just 2 to 3 losses away from elimination. Strengthening your board now to prevent even one loss directly improves your final placement. Spending your gold while you still have an HP buffer gives you room to recover, even if you lowroll your shops on your initial roll down. How If you're not confident in your roll speed, ignore the 50-gold interest breakpoint and start spending your gold gradually as your HP drops. Tips If you are confident that you can hit an unbeatable capped board that defeats every opponent in the lobby, you can greed your econ and hold onto your gold until the absolute last moment. title: TFTips - Position your main tank to protect your carry 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Position your main tank to protect your carry 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Position your main tank to protect your carry Intermediate Positioning What Position your main tank on the same side (left or right) as your carry. For melee carries (Fighters, etc.), place your main tank next to or in front of them. Why Your main tank can stall the longest, so you want to prevent enemy focus from reaching your main carry until your tank goes down. This ensures your carry stays safe and deals damage for as long as possible. If you place squishy units as a frontline in front of your carry, they'll get shredded immediately and won't provide meaningful protection. title: TFTips - Play around 2* 1-costs in the early game 【Teamfight Tactics】
text: TFTips - Play around 2* 1-costs in the early game 【Teamfight Tactics】 Skip to content Comp Tier List SET18 Tips Tools Team Builder Replays Play around 2* 1-costs in the early game Intermediate Progression What Slam items on your 2* 1-cost units and play around them in the early game. Why In the early game—especially throughout Stage 2—a 2* 1-cost is often the strongest unit on your board. Their upgraded base stats and ability scaling allow them to easily overpower un-upgraded champions early on. As a general rule of thumb, remember that a 2* 1-cost is slightly stronger than a 1* 3-cost filling the same role, and only falls slightly behind a 1* 4-cost. How Hold onto pairs of 1-cost units you find in the early game, especially during Stage 1. If you hit a 2* unit along the way, you can use to transfer items onto them.
